## Boundary and provenance checks

- The empty category, identity comonad, zero object, and degenerate equal-object cases introduce no exception in the eight comonad-side items.
- For the free-monoid Kleisli witness, \(X=\varnothing\) gives one endomorphism and every nonempty \(X\), including a singleton, gives infinitely many; the two-element idempotent monoid has exactly two. Hence no equivalence can exist.
- For the topology witness, empty and singleton sets have coincident discrete and indiscrete topologies; two points are the first valid nonconservative witness.
- A free word monoid on zero generators has one element, while one or more generators give an infinite monoid, so the two-element algebra is genuinely non-free up to isomorphism.
- None of the assigned Statements is an iff requiring a missing direction, and no family-choice assumption occurs.
- No assigned item targets an `ai-generated` Statement or Construction in `deps`. All four AI-generated refutations were checked independently.
- The extremal order is correct: co-Eilenberg–Moore factors into every comonad resolution, and every resolution factors into co-Kleisli. This agrees with the opposite of Riehl’s Kleisli-initial/Eilenberg–Moore-terminal result in [Category Theory in Context](https://emilyriehl.github.io/files/context.pdf).
